title: Golden GPU Node Image Checklist (build + promotion + rollback) — Dedicated Fleet
content:
Doc owner: Sahana
Last pass: aligned to Provision-to-Ready automation sprint (Dedicated bring-up). This is the checklist we run before an image is eligible for staging/prod promotion.

=== 0) Scope / assumptions ===
- This checklist is for the “golden” GPU node image used by Dedicated pools (and internal staging pools) in the provision-to-ready pipeline.
- Image is versioned, signed, and referenced by the fleet-provisioner orchestration + Terraform outputs.
- We support heterogeneous SKUs/regions; avoid assumptions that only work on one GPU family.

Definitions (quick):
- BUILD: creating a new image artifact (base OS + drivers + baseline hardening).
- VALIDATE: smoke tests + GPU health + kube bootstrap viability + runtime prereqs.
- PROMOTE: marking an image version eligible for staging/prod usage.
- ROLLBACK: reverting to previously-known-good image and draining/replacing nodes.

=== 1) Pre-flight checks (before starting a build) ===
[ ] Confirm reason for new image (security patch? driver bump? kernel bump? provisioning failure root cause? new SKU enablement?). Capture in change note.
[ ] Confirm target environments:
    - staging pools: yes/no
    - prod dedicated: yes/no
    - new region(s): list
    - new SKU(s): list
[ ] Confirm compatibility targets:
    - runtime chart versions pinned in redwood-helm-charts (see PR/commit)
    - nvidia-container-toolkit requirements
    - k8s minor version target (if pinned)
[ ] Confirm capacity impact window for promotion (pilot windows already agreed?): owner = Vanessa/Harish
[ ] Confirm artifact mirror status if using regional mirrors (known footgun: slow imaging due to mirror lag).

=== 2) Versioning + naming ===
[ ] Allocate new image version (monotonic, semver-ish). Format we’ve been using:
    - ri-gpu-golden-YYYYMMDD.N (e.g., ri-gpu-golden-20250306.1)
[ ] Record base OS + kernel + driver versions in the changelog section below.
[ ] Ensure previous version is still available and not garbage-collected (needed for rollback).

Changelog (fill in each build):
- Image version:
- Base OS (distro + release):
- Kernel version:
- NVIDIA driver version:
- CUDA toolkit/runtime (if included):
- nvidia-container-toolkit:
- Mellanox OFED / rdma-core (if applicable):
- Security patches applied / CVEs addressed:
- Notes on SKU/region specifics:

=== 3) Drivers + GPU runtime prerequisites ===
Goal: the image boots cleanly and can run containerized workloads with GPUs reliably.

NVIDIA driver:
[ ] Driver installed via approved mechanism (package repo vs. runfile). Prefer reproducible package install.
[ ] Driver version pinned and recorded (avoid floating latest).
[ ] Validate basic driver health:
    - command: nvidia-smi
    - expected: all GPUs listed; no “Driver/library version mismatch”; no persistent Xid spam.
[ ] Validate NVML works in container context:
    - command: docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
    - expected: nvidia-smi output inside container.

nvidia-container-toolkit:
[ ] Version pinned and recorded.
[ ] Confirm /etc/nvidia-container-runtime/config.toml is present + default runtime configured if required.

CUDA/NCCL (only if baked into image; otherwise verify runtime container provides it):
[ ] If CUDA libs present: confirm expected version strings.
[ ] If NCCL present: confirm version + that it matches runtime expectations.

RDMA / networking (if we claim support for multi-node or RDMA-enabled SKUs):
[ ] Validate OFED/rdma-core presence (if expected for target region/SKU).
[ ] Confirm no boot-time dmesg noise indicating NIC driver mismatch.

=== 4) Kernel params + OS settings (known footguns) ===
[ ] Cgroups mode matches k8s + runtime expectation (document if cgroupv2 is enabled).
[ ] Hugepages policy documented (if set). Ensure not breaking general workloads.
[ ] IOMMU / PCI settings:
    - confirm no GPU enumeration issues in dmesg
[ ] Disable sleep/hibernation on nodes.
[ ] Time sync present (chrony/systemd-timesyncd) and enabled.

Recommended quick checks:
- uname -r
- cat /proc/cmdline
- dmesg --level=err,warn | tail -n 200
- systemctl is-active chronyd || systemctl is-active systemd-timesyncd

=== 5) Security hardening + provenance ===
NOTE: This is the gating section for promotion to prod.

Base hardening:
[ ] SSH: disable password auth; only key-based.
[ ] SSH: root login disabled (or explicitly justified and documented).
[ ] Ensure default users / vendor accounts removed or locked.
[ ] Firewall baseline applied (as per infra standard); inbound minimized.
[ ] Disable unused services (bluetooth, avahi, etc.) on server images.
[ ] Audit logging enabled (auditd or equivalent) as per security guidance.

Secrets handling:
[ ] No baked-in secrets (tokens, kubeconfigs, cloud creds, private keys) present in image filesystem.
[ ] Verify cloud-init/user-data is used for per-pool secrets injection (not baked into AMI/image).

Supply chain:
[ ] Generate SBOM for image build output.
[ ] Artifact signing enabled (cosign or internal signer). Store signature + provenance metadata.
[ ] Vulnerability scan completed for OS packages + driver packages.
[ ] Security review sign-off required for:
    - kernel bump
    - driver bump
    - base OS major upgrade

Promotion gating sign-offs:
- Infra owner: ___________________
- Security approver (Marcus/Kevin): ___________________
- SRE (Rafael or delegate) for operational risk: ___________________

=== 6) Build steps (operator-facing, minimal) ===
(Exact commands vary by build pipeline; keep these steps high-level + link to runbook.)

[ ] Update build config (Packer/AMI pipeline/whatever we use) with pinned versions.
[ ] Kick off build in CI.
[ ] Confirm build logs show:
    - package install success
    - driver modules built/loaded without errors
    - signature step completed
    - SBOM uploaded
[ ] Capture build ID + artifact URL(s) for reference.

Artifacts to record:
- Image artifact ID (per cloud):
- Build job link:
- SBOM link:
- Signature/provenance link:

=== 7) Smoke tests (must-pass) ===
Run on a fresh instance created from the image (NOT the build runner).

System sanity:
[ ] Reboot test: reboot once; ensure services come back clean.
[ ] Disk space: ensure adequate space for logs/container cache.
[ ] DNS resolution works (basic + internal).
[ ] NTP/time sync working.

GPU health + diagnostics:
[ ] nvidia-smi (host)
[ ] dcgm diagnostics (if dcgm installed):
    - command: dcgmi discovery -l
    - optional: dcgmi diag -r 2
[ ] Verify no ECC/Xid errors at boot.

Container + runtime prereq:
[ ] docker/containerd present and healthy (depending on our node stack):
    - systemctl is-active containerd || systemctl is-active docker
[ ] Pull a standard runtime image from our registry (tests auth/mirrors):
    - docker pull <our-runtime-image-ref>

Kubernetes bootstrap sanity (if image includes kube prereqs):
[ ] kubelet can start (or at least packages/config are consistent).
[ ] CNI prerequisites present if expected.

Minimal inference smoke (only if we include local runtime bits; otherwise leave for provisioning validation stage):
[ ] Run a tiny GPU compute container to validate CUDA works:
    - docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-base-ubuntu22.04 bash -lc "python3 -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())'" (if torch is present)
    - If torch not present, skip and rely on canary perf suite.

=== 8) Performance/throughput sanity (recommended, not strictly required for image promotion) ===
We generally rely on the provisioning pipeline’s perf-canary readiness suite, but we still do a quick check on at least 1 node per new image version.

[ ] Run perf-canary “readiness suite” once on a node built from the new image.
[ ] Confirm output JSON stored and shows pass.
[ ] Compare to previous image baseline (no major regression). If regression, do not promote.

Notes:
- We’re not chasing top-line perf here; we’re catching broken driver/library configs and obvious regressions.

=== 9) Promotion checklist (staging -> prod) ===
Staging promotion:
[ ] Register image version as “eligible: staging” in the fleet-provisioner/control plane config.
[ ] Provision 1 internal staging pool with the new image (or expand an internal pool) and confirm provision-to-ready fully passes.
[ ] Validate time-to-ready stage breakdown: imaging step not worse than baseline (watch for mirror issues).
[ ] Validate readiness gates pass:
    - networking/DNS/TLS checks
    - GPU health checks
    - runtime smoke tests
    - perf-canary pass

Prod promotion:
[ ] Confirm all staging checks above pass + no open P0 issues.
[ ] Enable image version for prod usage (feature flag / allowlist if we have it).
[ ] Roll out to a small slice first:
    - 1 internal prod pool OR 1 low-risk customer expansion
    - monitor provisioning metrics + node health for at least N hours (fill in)
[ ] Announce promotion in #eng-infra with:
    - image version
    - changelog summary
    - known limitations
    - rollback steps

=== 10) Rollback notes (must be written BEFORE prod promotion) ===
Primary principle: rollback should be one control-plane config change + safe node replacement; no hand-editing nodes.

Rollback triggers (examples):
- Increased GPU Xid/ECC errors after rollout
- kubelet/container runtime instability
- perf-canary failure rate increases
- provisioning pipeline stuck in Imaging/Bootstrapping correlated to new image

Rollback steps (high level):
[ ] Stop new provisioning runs from selecting the bad image:
    - mark image version as “disabled” in control plane / remove from eligible list
[ ] Revert default image to previous-known-good version.
[ ] For pools already provisioned with bad image:
    - cordon/drain nodes (if applicable)
    - replace nodes via pool expansion/repair flow
    - verify Ready state only after readiness gates
[ ] File incident-style thread with:
    - image version
    - impact summary
    - mitigation
    - links to build artifacts + logs

Rollback info to fill in per image:
- Previous-known-good image version:
- Control plane config key(s) to flip:
- Runbook link:
- Oncall escalation:

=== 11) Notes / known issues / TODOs ===
- Known footgun: regional artifact mirror lag causing imaging step timeouts; if we see imaging > baseline, confirm mirror status and consider prewarm.
- If schema validation blocks a legitimate edge-case config during rollout, use break-glass only with audit log + explicit approval; do not permanently widen without follow-up.
- TODO: add an automated check in CI that ensures driver + toolkit versions match our supported runtime chart matrix.

Appendix A: quick copy/paste commands
- nvidia-smi
- dmesg --level=err,warn | tail -n 200
- systemctl status containerd --no-pager
- docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
- dcgmi discovery -l

Appendix B: escalation / owners
- Build pipeline support: Sahana
- Fleet automation: Vanessa / Gabe
- Security sign-off: Marcus / Kevin
- SRE readiness gates: Rafael / Aisha

(End)
